skill.name: pushing-to-notion
skill.description: Prepare one exact new Notion-backed record through portable Context meaning, current provider mapping, duplicate review, exact confirmation, single-use start, and read-after-write verification. Use for a supported configured record create; do not use for updates, deletion, sending, or another provider.
skill.shortDescription: Prepare and verify one exact configured record creation.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $pushing-to-notion to prepare this one configured record create without guessing fields, duplicating records, or bypassing review.

instructions: Resolve one portable record type, selected Notion integration mapping, exact configured instance authority, and current provider schema from the active lock.
Require the record type and every intended field to exist in the owning Context model and selected provider mapping.
Do not recover target identifiers from host prose, a legacy target mirror, or conversational memory.
flexibility: Ask for the missing portable record identity when the user has not selected one exact target.
stopConditions: Stop when the target, mapping, authority, schema, or exact current lock is missing or ambiguous.

instructions: Normalize requested values through the Context record contract before provider translation.
Match select, status, and multi-value options exactly against observed current options; resolve people and relations to exact provider-scoped identities.
Represent explicit empty values through the portable field contract and reject credentials, secret references, guessed options, and unsupported fields.
stopConditions: Stop when a required value is absent or any value cannot be represented by both Context and the selected provider mapping.

instructions: Use the record type's declared bounded deduplication fields and same-authority read capability before preparing a create.
Keep zero, one, and multiple candidates distinct and show exact candidate identities only in the private review boundary.
Route an existing record that needs change to the update workflow instead of overwriting it through create.
stopConditions: Stop the create when a duplicate candidate exists or the bounded duplicate check is unavailable or incomplete.

instructions: Prepare one immutable private record proposal with exact normalized values, target, deduplication requirement, expected effects, verification, and recovery boundary.
Expose only stable identifiers and fingerprints through sanitized inspection; keep human-readable values in selected-private review material.
For a batch request, preserve one exact proposed operation per record and report that provider effects are sequential rather than externally atomic.
flexibility: A human may review an explicitly itemized batch together, but each operation and selected subset remains fingerprint-bound.
stopConditions: Stop before approval when the exact provider compiler or read-after-write verifier is unavailable.

instructions: Create an expiring exact-scope approval request only from the immutable compiled batch and private review material.
Record exact operator confirmation separately, then consume it once into one deterministic durable checkpoint before any write.
Require a new request whenever input, subset, target, mapping, provider route, lock, or verification scope changes.
stopConditions: Stop when the resolved write policy prohibits the effect or when approval, confirmation, consumption, or checkpoint validation fails.

instructions: Re-run the exact duplicate-absence precondition immediately before the write, emit the approved create once, and capture only the normalized new identity.
Read the created identity back and verify every approved field and governed body fingerprint.
Treat transport or verification ambiguity as needs-attention; do not retry the create, invent deletion compensation, or claim rollback.
stopConditions: Stop and reconcile when provider state cannot prove exact success or exact absence.

verification: The exact portable record type, provider mapping, instance authority, schema, and lock are current.
Every field is valid in both Context and the selected Notion mapping, with no invented options or identities.
The bounded duplicate check proves exact absence immediately before create.
One exact confirmation is consumed once into one durable checkpoint.
The created record is read back and every approved field and body fingerprint matches.

gotchas.summary: A provider property label does not reveal whether the field is status, select, people, text, relation, or another type.
gotchas.countermeasure: Read the current schema and exact provider mapping before shaping any payload.

gotchas.summary: Supplying a missing option can create junk provider state or fail depending on provider settings.
gotchas.countermeasure: Accept only exact observed options unless a separate governed schema-change workflow is approved.

gotchas.summary: A create that skips its record-specific duplicate check can duplicate an existing record on first run or replay.
gotchas.countermeasure: Require a bounded same-authority absence check and never retry an ambiguous create.

gotchas.summary: Several provider creates do not become atomic merely because they share one human review.
gotchas.countermeasure: Checkpoint and verify each operation, report the exact completed prefix, and stop on the first ambiguity or failure.

gotchas.summary: Urgent language can pressure the operator boundary to treat a draft or blanket okay as write authority.
gotchas.countermeasure: Compress presentation when needed but retain the exact request, confirmation, single-use start, and verification boundary.

limitations: This guide intentionally replaces host-qualified direct writes with portable Context, Integration, approval, one-time start, checkpoint, and verification boundaries.
It remains a preview-only candidate and grants no provider call or write authority.
